hints: Focus on what type of oxide gives an alkaline solution with water, basic oxides do but acidic oxides do not.
Write what each remaining solid would form in water, then think about what its sulfate salt looks like with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.
Remember which Group 2 sulfate is famously insoluble and white, even though most Group 2 sulfates dissolve easily.
walkthrough:
**Use the first clue, alkaline solution**

W reacts with water to make $\text{OH}^-$ ions. That tells us W must be a basic oxide or a soluble hydroxide.

$$\text{basic oxide} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{metal hydroxide (alkaline)}$$

**Remove the acidic oxide**

Phosphorus oxide is a non-metal oxide. It reacts with water to form phosphoric acid, which is acidic not alkaline.

$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$$

**Use the second clue, white precipitate with sulfate**

Barium oxide reacts to give soluble barium hydroxide, a strong alkaline solution:
$$\text{BaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ba(OH)}_2$$ 
Then with dilute sulfuric acid it gives insoluble white barium sulfate:
$$\text{Ba}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4(\text{s})$$ 
Magnesium compounds give soluble $\text{MgSO}_4$, so no precipitate forms. This points to barium oxide.

options.A: Magnesium hydroxide is only very sparingly soluble, so it gives just a faintly alkaline suspension. More importantly, with $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ it forms $\text{MgSO}_4$, which is soluble, so no white precipitate would appear.
options.B: Magnesium oxide reacts with water to give $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$, which is sparingly soluble. With dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ it forms soluble $\text{MgSO}_4(aq)$, so you would see the solid dissolve, not a white precipitate.
options.C: Barium oxide is a basic oxide that dissolves to give strongly alkaline $\text{Ba(OH)}_2(aq)$. Addition of $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ ions then precipitates insoluble white $\text{BaSO}_4(s)$, which matches both observations perfectly.
options.D: Phosphorus oxide, such as $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, is an acidic oxide. It reacts with water to give an acidic solution of phosphoric acid, so it fails the first test of producing an alkaline solution.
